title: Review a setup plan
description: Read a plan as a review of sources, module selection, conflicts, and expected writes before applying a setup.

sections.title: What a plan is for
paragraphs: A plan gives you a concrete object to review before changing a machine. It connects the active blueprint, host, adapter, and module selection to the checks that smu can perform. Use it to catch a wrong checkout or unintended selection early.

A plan does not execute every shell script to predict its effects. A module may invoke a package manager, contact a service, or inspect the host when it runs. Read its implementation and trust metadata alongside the report.

sections.title: Start with sources and identity
paragraphs: Confirm that the blueprint checkout is the one you intended to use. Check its remote, branch or revision, and destination before interpreting later findings. Configuration from a different fork can be valid and still describe the wrong setup.

Distinguish the downloaded bootstrap installer from the CLI bundled in your blueprint. The bootstrap obtains the checkout; the pinned installer supplies the smu behavior you will use afterwards. Consult smu --help from that installed copy when a command differs from an example.

sections.title: Check the selected modules and adapter
paragraphs: Compare the proposed modules with the role of the target machine. A workstation collection can be inappropriate for a server even if it is available in the checkout. When using a built-in machine preset, inspect that preset and its platform requirements first.
If you use a named blueprint profile, preflight that exact profile and adapter. A valid profile name does not guarantee that every selected module publishes the required adapter implementation.

diagram.title: Review intent before execution
diagram.caption: Change the configuration when the intent is wrong, then generate the plan again.

sections.title: Interpret conflicts and unknown state
paragraphs: A conflict is a reason to inspect the source and destination, not to overwrite the destination immediately. Compare the content and decide which copy should be authoritative. Keep a backup before replacing a file you currently depend on.

Unknown installation state means detection is incomplete. It is not equivalent to missing, and it is not proof of failure. Check the module implementation and inspect the actual package, link, or application before deciding to run it again.
items: Read warnings about trust, secrets, and privilege use.
Check what rollback coverage actually includes.
Keep unresolved findings visible until you understand their consequence.

sections.title: Apply only the selection you reviewed
paragraphs: Keep the same checkout, host, and selection between review and execution. If you edit a profile, change a submodule revision, or switch machines, generate a fresh report. The previous report describes the previous inputs.

Begin with a small reviewed module or a test host. Read the command summary, inspect the changed path or installed tool, and then run the relevant doctor or status check. Record what you tested before expanding the setup.
